title: Urban Mixed-Use Design Challenge-Design a centrally located mixed-use building in Autodesk Revit with commercial spaces (Ground + 1st floor) and residential units (up to 8 floors). 1 Level of Basement (Car Parking + EV Charging), Total (B+G+9)(Note: Plot size and all required dimensions may be assumed by students (in mm units).
description:
• Description
• Facade-Driven Architectural Expression-Develop an innovative facade system that enhances architectural aesthetics, responds to climate (light, heat, ventilation), and blends with the surrounding urban context.
• Breathable & Nature-Integrated Design-Incorporate a central landscape courtyard and green interfaces (terraces, balconies) to create an airy, breathable structure that integrates nature and improves occupant well-being.
• Residential & Commercial Design Efficiency-Ensure functional planning for commercial activation on lower floors and well- designed residential units above, with optimal daylight, ventilation, privacy, and views.
• Structural Modeling & Detailing-Create 2D structural drawings for key components such as beams, columns, and slabs, including necessary detailing.The model should include all essential building elements: beams, columns, slabs, stairs, and tile flooring.
• Good to Have (Optional) - Site Compatibility & Environmental Analysis (Using Forma Site Design)-Utilize Forma Site Design to study site orientation, sun path, wind conditions,and massing strategies, ensuring the design is environmentally responsive and contextually appropriate. (1-2 Hour)
• High-Quality Visual Presentation & Walkthrough-Deliver a pictorial, design-focused presentation including rendered views, facade studies, diagrams, and a 30-second walkthrough animation.Rendering quality and visual storytelling will be key evaluation criteria.
• Participation Guidelines For Idea Submission:
• Each student team should submit Revit 3D Model of a Basement Parking + Ground + First Floor that creates a vibrant urban destination while seamlessly integrating nature, sustainability, and user well-being and a PowerPoint presentation (5-7 Slides).
• Models should be created using ONLY Revit and not copied or taken from any other source.
• AI Generated content is NOT ALLOWED.
For Grand Finale:
Students must use Autodesk Revit to design and create 3D Model of specific mixed used building within the given time period and present the following to the jury members:
Design a B+G+9 mixed-use development that brings together active commercial spaces and sustainable residential living. Create a nature-integrated, climate-responsive building centered around a landscaped courtyard that enhances daylight,ventilation, and occupant well-being.
Key Deliverables:
• Commercial podium (Basement Parking + Ground + First Floor) with retail, cafés,and community spaces.
• Residential levels (2nd–9th Floor) featuring efficient layouts, balconies, natural ventilation, and privacy.
• Innovative climate-responsive facade with shading elements and green terraces.
• Central landscaped courtyard as the project's defining feature.
• Complete Autodesk Revit model with architectural and structural elements,including detailed drawings.
• Optional Autodesk Forma studies for sun, wind, and environmental analysis.
• High-quality presentation with renders, diagrams, facade studies, and a 30-second walkthrough animation.
• PPT explaining the final project.
• Complete Structural reinforcement drawing of any one floor along with detailing.
• Complete 3D Model.
• Rendered images and Walkthrough video (30 secs.) of the final Model.
Note: Teams coming with pre-designed files will be disqualified.
• Attach Marking Criteria Table here*
• Faculty (SIH SPOC) Form Teams choosing to submit idea for Autodesk’s problem statement are required to request their faculty (SIH SPOC) to fill this 'Mandatory Form'.
• Autodesk Revit
• Autodesk Revit is a Building Information Modeling (BIM) software primarily used by architects, engineers, and construction professionals to design, model, and document buildings and infrastructure in 3D.
• Students and educators can click Here to get FREE access to Revit.
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on ai applied to a smart education problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Education. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on model, infrastructure. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 18/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Urban Mixed-Use Building Design in Autodesk Revit (B+G+9)

overview.in_plain_terms: Design (not code) a full mixed-use building, shops on the ground floors, apartments above, basement parking with EV charging, in Autodesk Revit, complete with a climate-responsive facade and full structural drawings.
overview.why_it_matters: This tests genuine architectural and BIM (Building Information Modeling) design skill, real skills needed to actually design buildings that work for both commerce and living, and respond intelligently to climate.
pain_points: Mixed-use buildings often don't successfully balance commercial ground-floor activation with residential upper-floor quality.
Facade design is often decorative rather than genuinely climate-responsive.
Structural detailing is frequently treated as an afterthought disconnected from architectural design.
overview.background: This is an Autodesk-sponsored architectural design challenge using Revit, requiring a complete mixed-use building design with structural detailing, not a software build.
overview.whats_being_asked: A complete B+G+9 mixed-use building design in Revit: commercial ground+1st floors, residential above, basement parking with EV charging, climate-responsive facade, structural drawings.
expected_solution: Complete architectural model (commercial, residential, parking, EV charging).
Central landscape courtyard and green interfaces.
Structural 2D drawings (beams, columns, slabs) with detailing.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Design/BIM submission format, evaluated on architectural design quality, climate-responsiveness, and structural detailing completeness, not software functionality.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Effort goes into genuine architectural design and Revit modeling across many building systems (architecture, structure, MEP-adjacent), a distinct skillset from coding.

competitive_landscape.level: Low crowding among typical hackathon teams
competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine architectural design skill and Revit proficiency specifically, a different pool of participants.

innovation.note: Judged on genuine facade/climate-response creativity and overall design coherence.

invention.note: Judged on modeling completeness across architecture and structure, plus real design detailing.

technical_feasibility.note: Achievable within 36 hours for a team with real Revit/architectural design experience; not achievable without it.

impact_and_benefits.note: About demonstrating genuine architectural and BIM design capability.

architecture.note: Not applicable in the software sense, this is a full architectural and structural design deliverable.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Only viable for a team with genuine Revit/architectural design experience. If your team has this capability, it's a well-specified, comprehensive design challenge covering both architecture and structure.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very comprehensive, clearly specified requirements (facade, courtyard, unit planning, structural detailing) give a rigorous, complete design target.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Attempting full B+G+9 detailing at genuinely high quality in 36 hours is ambitious even for a skilled team, prioritize the explicitly-weighted requirements (facade, structural detailing) over exhaustive completeness everywhere.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm real, hands-on Revit experience across both architectural modeling and structural drafting on your team before committing, this PS spans both disciplines.

idea_0_4: Confirm team Revit proficiency; if none, do not pursue this PS.
Define your plot dimensions and overall massing strategy, then sketch your facade concept and courtyard layout.
Split: one person on architectural modeling (units, commercial spaces), one on facade/courtyard design, one on structural detailing.
prototype_4_22: Model the overall building massing: basement parking/EV charging, ground+1st commercial, residential floors above.
Develop your facade system responding to climate (light, heat, ventilation) and the central courtyard/green interfaces.
Begin structural modeling: beams, columns, slabs, stairs.
integration_22_30: Complete residential unit planning with attention to daylight, ventilation, privacy, and views.
Complete 2D structural drawings and detailing for key components.
Optionally run Forma Site Design analysis for site orientation/sun path if time allows.
polish_30_36: Prepare clean renders of the facade, courtyard, and overall massing.
Prepare your structural drawing set for presentation.
Rehearse explaining your facade's climate-responsiveness rationale and unit-planning decisions.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Present your facade design with explicit climate-response reasoning, how specific elements respond to sun path, heat, and ventilation for this orientation, tied to real Forma analysis if you ran it, that grounded reasoning beats a facade that's decorative without functional justification.

strengths: Very comprehensive, clearly specified requirements give a complete design target.
Genuinely completable for a team with real Revit/architectural skill.
weaknesses: Completely inaccessible without genuine Revit and architectural design experience.
Full B+G+9 detailing at high quality is ambitious even for a skilled team in 36 hours.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: This PS is not viable without genuine Revit proficiency across architecture and structure.
team_fit.approach: Confirm tool proficiency across both disciplines before committing.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Not applicable, this is a BIM design deliverable requiring real hands-on tool skill.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: The entire architectural and structural design process, genuine design judgment that AI tooling doesn't substitute for.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: Not applicable in the typical sense, but attempting this without real Revit proficiency would produce an incomplete or unconvincing submission.

data_resource_availability.status: No dataset dependency, this is a design-skill and tool-proficiency challenge.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, if the team lacks Revit proficiency, this PS should not be selected.

judge_qna.question: How does your facade design actually respond to climate, beyond visual appearance?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through specific climate-response decisions, shading elements for sun path, ventilation strategy, and reference any Forma analysis you ran to validate these choices.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would you change about the facade for a different climate zone?

judge_qna.question: How did you balance commercial ground-floor activation with residential privacy above?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Discuss your specific planning decisions, floor transition design, acoustic/visual separation, access control between commercial and residential zones.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the biggest planning tradeoff you had to make in the unit layouts?
